messages:
Maya (PM): quick sync — we need to lock the prioritization matrix for the function/call surface. customers keep pushing for schema versioning + richer result shapes, but eng capacity is tight. can we decide launch gates for a minimum viable surface by end of next sprint?

Aj (ENG): I can propose a 3-level plan:
- level 0 (MVP): basic function invoke payload + sync response, small typed schema support (JSON Schema v4), simple success/error envelope
- level 1: structured output enforcement, schema validation on ingestion, telemetry + per-call latency/cost breakdowns
- level 2: orchestration features — async callbacks, retries, routing policies, and rollout flags (canary A/B)

Sophia (ENG-ML): +1. also need to call out model-side constraints: streaming partial results for long-running tool calls, and stable output formatting for evals. if we require strict schemas at L1, models need a fallback mode (a high-confidence vs low-confidence field) so downstream isn't blocked.

Ben (DESIGN): customers want predictable error states. proposal: standardize three error classes in the envelope: "user_error", "tool_error", "system_degraded". UX can show different remediation steps depending on class.

Maya (PM): good. can we make an explicit launch-gate checklist? small, actionable.

Aj (ENG): draft checklist: 
```
GATE: Function Invoke MVP
- API: /v1/invoke with body { model, input, tool_schema? }
- Response: { status: "ok|error", result: <opaque|string/object>, error_class? }
- Schema: accept JSON Schema refs, validate server-side, return validation warnings
- Telemetry: per-call latency, tokens_in/out, model_variant
- SLA: p99 < 1s for short calls (<=512 tokens)
- Security: allow opt-in payload redaction for hosted customers
- Docs: example payloads and best-practices
```

Sophia (ENG-ML): add: gating acceptance test: 5 replay prompts from customers with schema checks pass and quality regressions <= 2% compared to baseline.

Ben (DESIGN): add: gating UX test — sample error states mocked in console, and the retry UX flows work for at least two partner integrations.

Maya (PM): ok. priority matrix idea: x-axis = customer impact (pilot customers + revenue), y-axis = engineering complexity (est days). we should mark Level 1 items that unlock multiple customers (schema versioning, telemetry) as high impact even if medium complexity.

Aj (ENG): rough estimate: MVP 6 dev-weeks, L1 additional 4–6 weeks, L2 8+ weeks. depends on infra for async callbacks (ops will need to approve).

ops-bot: reminder: please file infra RFD for callback queueing, includes SLO targets and storage retention policy.

Maya (PM): next steps: Aj + Sophia to draft technical RFC for the 3-level plan by EOD Friday; Ben to sketch console error states by Wed; I'll align with two pilot customers to validate the gating checklist. can we capture owners on RFC?

Aj (ENG): I'll own the RFC + MVP implementation plan. Sophia will provide the eval criteria.

Sophia (ENG-ML): will attach the 5 replay prompts and baseline eval numbers.

Ben (DESIGN): I'll drop mockups in the RFC doc.

Maya (PM): perfect — if no objections, I'll create the RFC thread and assign reviewers. thanks all :thumbsup:

Aj (ENG): no objections. one ask: include a short example of a function schema we support, e.g.:
```
{
  "$id": "https://redwood.ai/schemas/booking-create.json",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "date": { "type": "string", "format": "date" },
    "party_size": { "type": "integer" },
    "notes": { "type": "string" }
  },
  "required": ["date", "party_size"]
}
```

Maya (PM): great, include that in the RFC and call out how we version schemas (semver vs url/id).

Sophia (ENG-ML): and add a note: when model outputs don't conform, system should emit "error_class: tool_error" + "confidence: <0.75>" so downstream can fall back to parsing heuristics.

Maya (PM): agreed. I'll open the RFC: 1769991111/rfc-function-invoke-prioritization later today. we can use this thread for quick clarifying q's.
